questions.stem: Agriculture is best defined as the
options: planting of food crops for family consumption only
rearing of livestock in the northern parts of Nigeria
buying and selling of farm produce in markets
cultivation of crops and rearing of animals for man's use, including processing and marketing of the products
questions.explanation: Agriculture covers crop and livestock production as well as processing, storage and marketing of products.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an importance of agriculture to the economy of a West African country?
options: Reduction of the population of farmers
Provision of raw materials for agro-based industries
questions.explanation: Agriculture supplies raw materials such as cocoa, cotton and palm oil to industries; it also provides food, employment and foreign exchange.

questions.topic: Problems of agricultural development and possible solutions
questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of agricultural development in Nigeria?
options: Abundant credit facilities for small-scale farmers
Availability of cheap and improved inputs
questions.explanation: Poor storage and processing cause heavy post-harvest losses; the other options would help, not hinder, development.

questions.topic: Problems of agricultural development and possible solutions
questions.stem: A suitable solution to the problem of land tenure that limits farm size in many communities is
options: encouraging fragmentation of land among family members
increasing the rate of bush burning
government acquisition and allocation of land to genuine farmers through land reform
questions.explanation: Land reform and allocation by government make larger, secure holdings available to farmers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of subsistence agriculture?
options: Production is mainly for family consumption with little surplus for sale
Use of large capital and hired labour
Production of a single crop on a large scale
Heavy use of machinery and modern technology
questions.explanation: Subsistence farming is small-scale, uses family labour and simple tools, and produces mainly for the household.

questions.stem: Commercial agriculture differs from subsistence agriculture in that commercial agriculture
options: aims mainly at profit and usually specialises in one or a few enterprises
depends only on simple farm tools
is practised on small, scattered plots
questions.explanation: Commercial farms are profit-oriented, large-scale and specialised, using hired labour and machinery.

questions.topic: Roles of government in agricultural development
questions.stem: Government can encourage agricultural production by
options: raising import duties on farm machinery
providing subsidised inputs such as fertilisers and improved seeds
questions.explanation: Subsidies, credit, research, extension and infrastructure are roles of government in agricultural development.

questions.topic: Roles of government in agricultural development
questions.stem: The International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) is located in
questions.explanation: IITA is in Ibadan; NRCRI is at Umudike, NCRI at Badeggi and NVRI at Vom.

questions.topic: Roles of government in agricultural development
questions.stem: Which research institute in Nigeria is mainly concerned with the improvement of oil palm?
options: National Root Crops Research Institute, Umudike
Cocoa Research Institute of Nigeria, Ibadan
Nigerian Institute for Oil Palm Research (NIFOR), near Benin City
questions.explanation: NIFOR, near Benin City, carries out research on oil palm and other palms.

questions.topic: Role of non-governmental organizations in agricultural development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a role of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in agricultural development?
options: Training farmers and providing small grants or inputs to rural communities
Fixing the prices of export crops
questions.explanation: NGOs support farmers through training, input supply, credit and community projects; law-making and taxation are government functions.

questions.stem: The Land Use Act of 1978 in Nigeria vested the ownership of land in each state in the
options: state governor, to hold in trust for the people
questions.explanation: The Act places land in each state under the control of the governor in trust for the people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of agricultural land reform?
options: It makes land more easily available to people who want to farm
questions.explanation: Land reform aims to improve access to land, reduce disputes and encourage investment.

questions.topic: Meaning and importance of agricultural ecology
questions.stem: Knowledge of agricultural ecology helps a farmer to
options: choose crops and animals suited to the environmental conditions of the area
questions.explanation: Matching crops and livestock to climate and soil improves productivity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-agricultural use of land?
questions.explanation: Industry, housing, roads and mining are non-agricultural uses; crops, pastures and forests are agricultural.

questions.stem: Land as a factor of production is described as fixed in supply because
options: it can be moved from one place to another
its total quantity cannot be increased by man
questions.explanation: The total land area is fixed; only its productivity can be improved.

questions.topic: Factors affecting land availability for agricultural purpose
questions.stem: Which of the following factors reduces the availability of land for agriculture?
questions.explanation: Expansion of towns, roads and industries takes over farmland.

questions.topic: Factors affecting land availability for agricultural purpose
questions.stem: The communal land tenure system can limit agricultural development mainly because
options: land is owned by the government
individual farmers do not have secure title to use the land as collateral for loans
it allows land to be sold freely
questions.explanation: Without individual title, farmers cannot use land as security for credit and may not invest in long-term improvements.

questions.topic: Agro-allied industries and relationship between agriculture and industry
questions.stem: Which of the following is an agro-allied industry that uses cassava as raw material?
questions.explanation: Cassava is processed into garri, starch, flour and ethanol.

questions.topic: Agro-allied industries and relationship between agriculture and industry
questions.stem: Industry contributes to agriculture by
options: supplying farm inputs such as fertilisers, machinery and agrochemicals
providing raw materials such as cotton lint
questions.explanation: Industries manufacture inputs used by farmers; agriculture in turn supplies raw materials and food to industry.

questions.topic: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production
questions.stem: Which of the following crops is best suited to the humid rainforest zone of West Africa?
questions.explanation: Cocoa requires high rainfall, humidity and shade found in the rainforest; millet and sorghum suit the savanna.

questions.topic: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production
questions.stem: Cattle production is concentrated in the northern savanna of Nigeria mainly because
options: there is more rainfall in the north
the tsetse fly that transmits trypanosomiasis is less common there
cattle cannot drink water in the south
questions.explanation: Tsetse flies thrive in humid forest areas; the drier savanna has fewer tsetse and plenty of grazing.

questions.topic: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production
questions.stem: Which of the following is a biotic factor affecting crop production?
questions.explanation: Biotic factors are living organisms such as pests, pathogens, weeds and soil organisms.

questions.topic: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production
questions.stem: Photoperiodism in crops refers to the response of plants to
options: the length of day (duration of light)
questions.explanation: Short-day and long-day plants flower in response to day length.

questions.stem: Rocks formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma are called
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks such as granite and basalt form from cooled magma or lava.

questions.stem: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from
questions.explanation: Heat and pressure change limestone into marble; sandstone becomes quartzite and shale becomes slate.

questions.stem: Which of the following rocks is sedimentary?
questions.explanation: Sandstone forms from compacted sand grains; basalt and granite are igneous and gneiss is metamorphic.

questions.stem: The breakdown of rocks by the action of water, temperature changes and wind without change in chemical composition is called
questions.explanation: Physical (mechanical) weathering breaks rock into smaller pieces without chemical change.

questions.stem: Carbonation is a chemical weathering process in which
options: water freezes in cracks and expands
carbonic acid in rain water dissolves rocks such as limestone
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide dissolves in rain to form carbonic acid, which reacts with calcium carbonate.

questions.stem: In a soil profile, the horizon in which materials leached from above accumulate is the
questions.explanation: The B horizon is the zone of illuviation where clay, iron and aluminium compounds accumulate.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors of soil formation refers to the shape of the land surface?
questions.explanation: Topography affects drainage, erosion and depth of soil.

questions.topic: Types, composition and properties of soil
questions.stem: The four main components of soil are
options: mineral matter, organic matter, water and air
questions.explanation: Soil consists of mineral particles, organic matter, soil water and soil air.

questions.topic: Types, composition and properties of soil
questions.stem: A soil that is gritty to the touch, drains rapidly and has low water-holding capacity is
questions.explanation: Sandy soils have large particles and pores, so water drains quickly.

questions.topic: Types, composition and properties of soil
questions.stem: Loamy soil is considered the best for crop production because it
options: has a good balance of sand, silt and clay with good drainage, aeration and water retention
is made up of only clay particles
questions.explanation: Loam combines the drainage of sand with the nutrient and water holding of clay.

questions.topic: Types, composition and properties of soil
questions.stem: A soil sample has a pH of 4.5. The farmer can correct this condition by applying
questions.explanation: pH 4.5 is strongly acidic; lime (calcium carbonate) raises pH. Ammonium sulphate and sulphur make soil more acidic.

questions.topic: Types, composition and properties of soil
questions.stem: Soil particles with a diameter of less than 0.002 mm are classified as
questions.explanation: Clay particles are smaller than 0.002 mm in both the international and USDA systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following nutrients is mainly responsible for vigorous vegetative growth and dark green colour in plants?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a constituent of proteins and chlorophyll; deficiency causes yellowing and stunting.

questions.stem: Phosphorus is important to crops because it
options: is the central atom of chlorophyll
promotes root development and early maturity
questions.explanation: Phosphorus aids root growth, flowering, seed formation and early maturity.

questions.stem: A farmer wants to apply 60 kg of nitrogen per hectare using NPK 15:15:15. The quantity of the fertiliser needed per hectare is
questions.explanation: NPK 15:15:15 contains 15% N. Quantity = 60 / 0.15 = 400 kg.

questions.stem: How much urea (46% N) is required to supply 92 kg of nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Urea needed = 92 / 0.46 = 200 kg.

questions.stem: After several seasons of heavy rainfall on a sandy farm, a farmer noticed nitrogen deficiency in his maize even though he applied nitrogen fertiliser every year. The most likely cause is
options: leaching of soluble nitrates below the root zone
questions.explanation: Nitrates are very soluble and are washed down quickly through porous sandy soils; fixation and mulching add or conserve nutrients.

questions.stem: The method of irrigation in which water is applied slowly to the root zone through small pipes and emitters is
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water drop by drop at the roots, saving water.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of overhead sprinkler irrigation is that it
options: cannot be used on uneven land
loses much water by evaporation and may encourage leaf diseases
uses less water than drip irrigation
questions.explanation: Sprinklers wet foliage and lose water to wind and evaporation; they can be used on uneven land.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem associated with irrigation in dry areas if drainage is poor?
options: Accumulation of salts in the soil (salinisation)
Leaching of salts from the soil
questions.explanation: Evaporation of irrigation water leaves salts that accumulate when drainage is poor.

questions.stem: Drainage of agricultural land is the
options: addition of water to the soil
levelling of the land with a grader
removal of excess water from the soil
questions.explanation: Drainage removes excess water to improve aeration and root growth.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of poor drainage on crops?
options: Poor aeration of the root zone
Increased activity of aerobic soil organisms
questions.explanation: Waterlogging fills pores with water, depriving roots of oxygen.

questions.stem: Run-off of excess nitrogen and phosphate fertilisers from farms into streams can cause
questions.explanation: Nutrient enrichment causes algal blooms; their decay depletes oxygen and kills fish.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way to reduce pollution from agricultural chemicals?
options: Burning empty pesticide containers in open fields
Following label instructions and using integrated pest management
questions.explanation: Correct dosage, IPM and proper disposal reduce contamination of water, soil and air.

questions.stem: Which of the following farm tools is used for transplanting seedlings?
questions.explanation: A hand trowel lifts seedlings with a ball of soil and digs small planting holes.

questions.stem: A sickle is mainly used for
options: harvesting cereals such as rice and cutting grass
questions.explanation: The curved blade of a sickle cuts stalks of rice, wheat and grasses.

questions.stem: To prevent rusting of farm tools after use, they should be
options: cleaned, dried and oiled before storage
questions.explanation: Cleaning and oiling metal parts prevents rust.

questions.stem: A disc harrow is used on the farm to
options: break clods and level the soil after ploughing
questions.explanation: Harrowing is secondary tillage to break clods and produce a fine tilth.

questions.stem: Which of the following implements is used for primary tillage?
questions.explanation: Primary tillage opens the soil; ploughs (disc or mouldboard) are primary tillage implements.

questions.stem: A combine harvester performs which of the following operations?
options: Cutting, threshing and cleaning of grain
questions.explanation: A combine harvester reaps, threshes and winnows grain in one operation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a daily maintenance practice for a tractor?
options: Checking the engine oil and radiator water levels
questions.explanation: Daily checks include oil, coolant, fuel, tyre pressure and greasing points.

questions.stem: A precaution that should be taken when operating a tractor is to
options: refuel while the engine is running
avoid carrying passengers on the tractor
drive across steep slopes at high speed
questions.explanation: Passengers, refuelling with the engine on and steep slopes cause accidents.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a limitation to agricultural mechanisation in West Africa?
questions.explanation: Fragmented holdings, high costs, lack of spare parts and skilled operators limit mechanisation.

questions.stem: Which of the following would improve the prospects of agricultural mechanisation in Nigeria?
options: Banning the importation of spare parts without local alternatives
Establishing tractor hiring services and local fabrication of implements
questions.explanation: Hire services and local manufacture reduce cost and improve access to machines.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most widely used source of farm power on small-scale farms in West Africa?
questions.explanation: Most smallholders rely on human labour with hoes and cutlasses.

questions.stem: An advantage of animal power over human power is that animals
options: can do heavier work and cover larger areas in a given time
do not need to be fed
can be used in all parts of the forest zone without risk
questions.explanation: Draught animals provide more power, though they need feeding and care and are limited by tsetse in forest areas.

questions.stem: In a four-stroke engine, the correct order of strokes is
questions.explanation: The cycle is suck (induction), squeeze (compression), bang (power), blow (exhaust).

questions.stem: Which instrument is used for measuring horizontal angles and bearings in farm surveying?
questions.explanation: A prismatic compass gives bearings; ranging poles mark lines and arrows count chain lengths.

questions.stem: A rectangular farm measures 250 m by 120 m. Its area in hectares is
The Gunter's chain used in land surveying is
options: 100 m long and divided into 10 links
30 m long and divided into 150 links
66 feet (about 20.1 m) long and divided into 100 links
22 feet long and divided into 50 links
questions.explanation: A Gunter's chain is 66 ft (20.12 m) with 100 links.

questions.stem: In planning a farm, the first consideration should usually be
options: the colour of the farm buildings
the position of the farmer's house in the village
the objectives of the farmer and the resources available
questions.explanation: Farm planning begins with goals, capital, land, labour and market considerations.

questions.stem: Which of the following should be considered when choosing a site for a farm?
questions.explanation: Access to markets and roads, soil quality, water and topography guide farm siting.

questions.stem: In siting a poultry house on a farmstead, the length of the house should run
options: north to south to allow maximum sunlight inside
east to west to reduce direct sunlight entering the house
in any direction since it does not matter
questions.explanation: East-west orientation reduces direct sun on the long walls, keeping the house cooler.

questions.stem: Farm buildings for livestock should be sited away from the farmer's residence and downwind of it mainly to
options: reduce the effect of odour and noise and the spread of diseases to people
questions.explanation: Siting downwind and at a distance limits smell, flies, noise and zoonotic risk.

questions.stem: Which of the following crops is classified as a legume?
questions.explanation: Groundnut belongs to the family Fabaceae (Leguminosae); sorghum is a cereal, cassava a root crop and okra a vegetable.

questions.stem: Based on life cycle, cassava, which can remain in the soil for more than one year before harvest, is described as
questions.explanation: Cassava can be harvested from about 9 months up to 2-3 years; it is perennial, though often managed as an annual.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a beverage crop?
questions.explanation: Cocoa, coffee and tea are beverage crops; cotton is a fibre, rubber a latex and oil palm an oil crop.

questions.stem: The botanical name of maize is
questions.explanation: Zea mays is maize; Oryza sativa is rice, Sorghum bicolor is guinea corn and Manihot esculenta is cassava.

questions.stem: Cassava is commonly propagated by
questions.explanation: Stem cuttings of about 20-30 cm are planted; seeds are used only in breeding.

questions.stem: Maize is planted at a spacing of 75 cm x 25 cm with one plant per stand. The plant population per hectare is
The setts used for planting yam are obtained from
options: tubers cut into pieces or small whole tubers (seed yams)
questions.explanation: Yam is propagated vegetatively from setts (pieces of tuber) or seed yams.

questions.stem: In cocoa production, the young plants are shaded in the early years mainly because they
options: need to be protected from flooding
are attacked by rodents in sunlight
are sensitive to direct sunlight and drying out
questions.explanation: Young cocoa needs shade from plantain, cocoyam or forest trees to reduce sun scorch and water loss.

questions.stem: Fermentation of cocoa beans after harvesting is done to
options: develop the flavour and colour of the beans and kill the embryo
increase the weight of the beans
questions.explanation: Fermentation kills the seed, removes pulp and develops the chocolate flavour precursors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an important cultural practice in rice production in lowland fields?
options: Removing all water from the field before planting
Maintaining a controlled level of water in the field (puddling and flooding)
questions.explanation: Lowland (paddy) rice is grown in puddled, flooded fields with controlled water depth.

questions.stem: Tapping is a harvesting operation carried out in
questions.explanation: Latex is obtained by cutting thin slices of bark (tapping) on the rubber tree.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a forage legume?
questions.explanation: Centrosema is a legume; the others are grasses (guinea grass, elephant grass, gamba grass).

questions.stem: Mixing grasses and legumes in a pasture is advantageous because the legumes
options: reduce the palatability of the pasture
fix nitrogen and improve the protein content of the forage
questions.explanation: Legumes add nitrogen to the soil and supply protein to grazing animals.

questions.stem: The main aim of crop improvement is to
options: increase the number of weeds in the farm
reduce the food value of crops
develop varieties with higher yield, better quality and resistance to pests and diseases
questions.explanation: Breeders select for yield, quality, earliness, drought tolerance and pest/disease resistance.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods of crop improvement involves crossing two genetically different parents?
questions.explanation: Hybridisation combines desirable traits of two parents; selection only picks from existing variation.

questions.stem: Bringing in a crop variety from another country and testing it for local adaptation is called
questions.explanation: Plant introduction brings in new varieties, which are then screened under local conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a forest management practice?
options: Selective exploitation and regeneration of trees
Clearing forest for road construction without replanting
questions.explanation: Selective felling, regeneration, fire protection and forest reserves sustain forest resources.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a timber species of the Nigerian rainforest?
questions.explanation: Iroko is a valuable rainforest hardwood; shea, neem and baobab are savanna trees.

questions.stem: The practice in which farmers grow food crops between rows of young forest trees until the canopy closes is called
questions.explanation: In taungya, farmers tend young plantation trees while cropping between them.

questions.stem: In alley cropping, fast-growing leguminous shrubs such as Leucaena and Gliricidia are planted in hedgerows mainly to
options: supply prunings that serve as mulch and green manure for the crops between the rows
questions.explanation: Hedgerow prunings add organic matter and nitrogen and suppress weeds.

questions.topic: Meaning and importance of ornamental plants
questions.stem: Ornamental plants are grown mainly for
options: their beauty and to improve the appearance of the surroundings
questions.explanation: Ornamentals beautify homes, offices and public places; some also provide shade and windbreaks.

questions.topic: Meaning and importance of ornamental plants
questions.stem: Which of the following is an economic importance of ornamental plants?
options: They are the main source of carbohydrate
They provide fibre for textile industries
They provide income to people who run flower nurseries and landscaping businesses
They are used to feed poultry
questions.explanation: Nurseries, florists and landscapers earn income from ornamentals.

questions.stem: Which of the following is commonly used as a lawn grass?
questions.explanation: Carpet grass and Bahama grass form low, dense turf suitable for lawns.

questions.stem: Which of the following ornamental plants is commonly used for hedges?
questions.explanation: Ixora, Duranta and Hibiscus are popular hedge plants.

questions.topic: Settings and location for planting ornamental plants
questions.stem: Ornamental trees with large spreading roots should NOT be planted
options: very close to buildings and underground pipes
questions.explanation: Roots of large trees can crack foundations and damage drains and pipes.

questions.stem: Marcotting (air layering) involves
options: inducing roots on a branch while it is still attached to the parent plant
joining a scion to a rootstock
inserting a bud under the bark of a stock
questions.explanation: The bark is ringed, wrapped with moist medium and polythene; roots form before the branch is cut off.

questions.stem: Budding as a method of propagation involves
options: burying a branch in the soil
inserting a bud from a desired plant into the bark of a rootstock
sowing seeds in a seed box
questions.explanation: In budding a single bud (scion) is inserted into a T-shaped cut on the stock.

questions.stem: Regular cutting of a hedge to maintain its shape is called
questions.explanation: Trimming encourages dense growth and keeps the hedge neat.

questions.stem: A cocoa farmer in Ondo State observes that many pods turn brown, then black, and rot during the peak of the rainy season. The cause and a suitable control measure are
options: a virus; cut out and burn the affected trees
a fungus (Phytophthora); remove infected pods and spray copper-based fungicide
a bacterium; inject antibiotics into the trunk
questions.explanation: Black pod is caused by Phytophthora species and favoured by wet weather; sanitation and copper fungicides control it.

questions.stem: Farmers are advised to take cassava cuttings only from symptom-free plants because cassava mosaic disease is spread both by infected cuttings and by
questions.explanation: Cassava mosaic viruses are carried in stem cuttings and transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci.

questions.stem: Maize streak disease is caused by a virus transmitted by
questions.explanation: Maize streak virus is spread by Cicadulina leafhoppers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cultural method of controlling crop diseases?
options: Crop rotation and use of resistant varieties
questions.explanation: Cultural control uses farm practices such as rotation, sanitation and resistant varieties.

questions.stem: The pest that bores into the stems of maize, causing dead heart and lodging, is the
questions.explanation: Larvae of stem borers tunnel in maize stems, weakening them.

questions.stem: The cassava mealybug in West Africa was successfully controlled by the introduction of a
questions.explanation: This is a classic example of biological control by IITA and partners using a parasitoid wasp.

questions.stem: The insect pest that damages stored cowpea grains by making round holes in them is the
questions.explanation: Bruchid larvae develop inside cowpea seeds and the adults emerge through round holes.

questions.stem: Insects with piercing and sucking mouthparts, such as aphids, are best controlled with
options: stomach poisons applied on the soil
questions.explanation: Systemic insecticides move in the sap and kill sap-sucking insects.

questions.stem: A weed is best defined as
options: a plant growing where it is not wanted
a plant that has no flowers
questions.explanation: Any plant out of place, competing with crops, is a weed.

questions.stem: Spear grass (Imperata cylindrica) is difficult to control mainly because it
questions.explanation: Rhizomes regrow after slashing or burning, so systemic herbicides or repeated tillage are needed.

questions.stem: Striga (witchweed) is a weed of cereals that
options: is parasitic, attaching to the roots of the host
questions.explanation: Striga attaches to roots of sorghum, maize and millet and draws water and nutrients.

questions.topic: Types and classification of farm animals
questions.stem: Which of the following farm animals is a ruminant?
questions.explanation: Goats chew the cud and have a four-chambered stomach; pigs, rabbits and fowls are non-ruminants.

questions.topic: Types and classification of farm animals
questions.stem: The White Fulani (Bunaji) is a breed of
questions.explanation: White Fulani is a Zebu cattle breed of northern Nigeria.

questions.topic: Types and classification of farm animals
questions.stem: Which of the following breeds of cattle is trypanotolerant?
questions.explanation: N'Dama and Muturu tolerate trypanosomiasis and can be kept in tsetse areas.

questions.topic: Anatomy and physiology of farm animals
questions.stem: The true stomach of a ruminant, where gastric juice is secreted, is the
questions.explanation: The abomasum secretes digestive enzymes and acid; the other compartments are fermentation and filtering chambers.

questions.topic: Anatomy and physiology of farm animals
questions.stem: In the domestic fowl, food is softened and stored before digestion in the
questions.explanation: The crop stores and moistens food; the gizzard grinds it.

questions.stem: The gestation period of a sow is approximately
questions.explanation: Sows farrow after about 114 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days); cows take about 283 days.

questions.stem: The act of giving birth in goats is called
questions.explanation: Goats kid, pigs farrow, cows calve and rabbits kindle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign of heat (oestrus) in a cow?
options: Mounting other cows and standing to be mounted, with a clear mucus discharge
questions.explanation: Restlessness, mounting, standing heat, bellowing and mucus discharge are heat signs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effect of high environmental temperature on poultry?
options: Reduced feed intake and egg production
questions.explanation: Heat stress reduces feed intake, growth and egg production and causes thin-shelled eggs.

questions.stem: Farm animals adapted to hot climates usually have
options: heavy fat deposits under the skin all over the body
short, light-coloured, glossy coats and loose skin
questions.explanation: Light glossy coats reflect heat; loose skin and large ears increase heat loss.

questions.stem: The system of poultry management in which birds are kept on a floor covered with wood shavings is the
questions.explanation: In the deep litter system birds move freely on litter material inside a house.

questions.stem: Piglets are given iron injections within the first week of birth to prevent
questions.explanation: Sow's milk is low in iron and piglets reared indoors develop iron-deficiency anaemia.

questions.stem: A feed that is high in fibre and low in digestible nutrients, such as hay, is classified as a
questions.explanation: Roughages (hay, silage, straw) are bulky and fibrous; concentrates are energy- or protein-rich.

questions.stem: Which of the following feedstuffs is a protein concentrate?
questions.explanation: Oilseed cakes such as groundnut and soybean cake are high in protein.

questions.stem: Using the Pearson square, a farmer wants to mix maize (9% crude protein) and soybean meal (44% crude protein) to make a ration with 18% crude protein. The parts of maize to soybean meal needed are
options: 9 parts maize to 26 parts soybean meal
26 parts maize to 9 parts soybean meal
18 parts maize to 35 parts soybean meal
44 parts maize to 9 parts soybean meal
questions.explanation: Maize parts = 44 - 18 = 26; soybean meal parts = 18 - 9 = 9.

questions.stem: A maintenance ration is fed to animals to
options: keep them alive and maintain body weight without production
questions.explanation: Maintenance ration covers basic body functions; production rations are additional.

questions.stem: The number of animals that a unit area of pasture can support without deterioration is the
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity is the maximum number the pasture can sustain over a period.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of improving natural rangeland?
options: Reseeding with improved grasses and legumes and rotational grazing
questions.explanation: Reseeding, fertilising, controlled burning and rotational grazing improve range productivity.

questions.stem: Mating of closely related animals, such as father and daughter, is called
questions.explanation: Inbreeding increases homozygosity; it can fix traits but may cause inbreeding depression.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of artificial insemination?
options: Semen from one superior bull can be used to serve many cows, even at distant places
It increases the spread of venereal diseases
It does not require trained personnel
It needs the bull to be present on every farm
questions.explanation: AI spreads superior genes widely, reduces cost of keeping males and limits disease spread.

questions.stem: Newcastle disease of poultry is caused by a
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease is viral and controlled by vaccination.

questions.stem: Coccidiosis in poultry, which causes bloody droppings, is caused by
questions.explanation: Eimeria species damage the intestinal lining; coccidiostats are used for control.

questions.stem: Which of the following diseases of cattle is spread by the tsetse fly?
questions.explanation: Trypanosomes are transmitted by tsetse flies (Glossina).

questions.stem: Abortion in cattle, goats and pigs, which can also infect humans who drink unpasteurised milk, is a sign of
questions.explanation: Brucellosis is a bacterial zoonosis causing abortion and infertility.

questions.stem: Which of the following fish species is commonly cultured in ponds in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Clarias and Tilapia are the main pond-cultured species in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Lime is applied to a fish pond before stocking mainly to
options: correct acidity and improve water quality
questions.explanation: Liming raises pH, improves alkalinity and helps disinfect the pond bottom.

questions.stem: In a honeybee colony, the only fertile female is the
questions.explanation: The queen lays all the eggs; workers are sterile females and drones are males.

questions.stem: Smoke is used when opening a beehive in order to
options: calm the bees and reduce stinging
questions.explanation: Smoke masks alarm pheromones and makes bees gorge on honey, so they become less aggressive.

questions.stem: The law of diminishing returns states that as more units of a variable input are added to a fixed input,
options: total output always increases at an increasing rate
the additional output from each extra unit eventually decreases
the cost of production remains constant
questions.explanation: Beyond a point, each extra unit of variable input adds less to output (marginal product declines).

questions.stem: Opportunity cost is best explained as
options: the total cost of running a farm
the money borrowed from a bank
the value of the next best alternative forgone when a choice is made
questions.explanation: A farmer who uses land for maize forgoes the cassava that could have been grown there.

questions.stem: A farmer used 1, 2, 3 and 4 bags of fertiliser on equal plots and obtained 10, 18, 24 and 27 bags of maize respectively. The marginal product of the 4th bag of fertiliser is
questions.explanation: Marginal product = 27 - 24 = 3 bags; the falling increments (10, 8, 6, 3) show diminishing returns.

questions.stem: The reward for capital as a factor of production is
questions.explanation: Land earns rent, labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur earns profit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of capital in agriculture?
options: A tractor owned by the farmer
questions.explanation: Capital is man-made wealth used in production, such as machines, buildings and money.

questions.stem: The entrepreneur in farm business is the person who
options: organises the other factors of production and bears the risk
questions.explanation: The entrepreneur combines land, labour and capital and takes the risk of loss.

questions.stem: The law of demand states that, other things being equal,
options: the higher the price, the higher the quantity demanded
price has no effect on quantity demanded
quantity demanded rises with the cost of production
the higher the price of a commodity, the lower the quantity demanded
questions.explanation: Price and quantity demanded vary inversely, so the demand curve slopes downwards.

questions.stem: When the price of garri rose from ₦400 to ₦500 per measure, the quantity demanded fell from 100 to 90 measures. The price elasticity of demand is
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity = 10%; percentage change in price = 25%; elasticity = 10/25 = 0.4.

questions.stem: Which of the following would cause the demand curve for eggs to shift to the right?
options: A fall in the price of eggs
An outbreak of disease reported to be spread by eggs
A rise in the price of eggs
questions.explanation: Higher income raises demand at every price; a change in the egg price only moves along the curve.

questions.stem: According to the law of supply, other things being equal,
options: more of a commodity is supplied at higher prices
less is supplied at higher prices
supply does not depend on price
supply falls when the cost of production falls
questions.explanation: Higher prices make production more profitable, so quantity supplied rises.

questions.stem: Which of the following would REDUCE the supply of tomatoes to the market?
options: An outbreak of a pest such as Tuta absoluta on tomato farms
questions.explanation: Pest outbreaks reduce output and shift the supply curve to the left; the others increase supply.

questions.topic: Implications of demand and supply for agricultural production
questions.stem: Prices of perishable farm produce such as tomatoes are usually low at the peak of the harvest season because
options: supply greatly exceeds demand at that time
demand is highest at that time
questions.explanation: A glut at harvest increases supply, depressing prices; better storage and processing can stabilise them.

questions.topic: Implications of demand and supply for agricultural production
questions.stem: Equilibrium price in a market is the price at which
questions.explanation: At equilibrium there is no shortage or surplus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of a farm manager?
options: Planning, organising and controlling farm operations
Fixing the prices of export crops
questions.explanation: Farm managers plan, organise, direct, coordinate, control and keep records.

questions.stem: The function of a farm manager that involves checking actual performance against plans and correcting deviations is
questions.explanation: Controlling compares results with targets and takes corrective action.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem faced by farm managers in West Africa?
questions.explanation: Weather risks, price instability, pests, inadequate credit and labour shortages trouble farm managers.

questions.stem: A farmer borrowed ₦600 000 from a bank at a simple interest rate of 12% per annum for 2 years. The total amount to be repaid is
Which of the following is a source of agricultural credit to farmers in Nigeria?
options: Bank of Agriculture and cooperative societies
questions.explanation: Specialised agricultural banks, commercial banks, cooperatives, money lenders and family are sources of credit.

questions.stem: One reason why small-scale farmers find it difficult to obtain loans from commercial banks is
options: too much capital of their own
low interest rates charged by banks
questions.explanation: Banks demand collateral such as land titles, which many smallholders lack.

questions.stem: A record of all the assets owned by a farm at a given time is the
questions.explanation: An inventory lists items such as land, buildings, machines, livestock and stores, with their values.

questions.stem: A tractor bought for ₦8 000 000 is expected to last 6 years with a scrap value of ₦800 000. Using the straight-line method, the annual depreciation is
questions.explanation: Depreciation = (cost - scrap value) / life = (8 000 000 - 800 000) / 6 = ₦1 200 000.

questions.stem: A poultry farmer sold eggs worth ₦2 500 000 in a year. Variable costs were ₦1 600 000 and fixed costs ₦400 000. The gross margin was
questions.explanation: Gross margin = revenue - variable costs = 2 500 000 - 1 600 000 = ₦900 000 (net profit would be ₦500 000).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of marketing of agricultural produce?
options: Storage, transportation and grading of produce
questions.explanation: Marketing functions include assembling, grading, processing, storage, transport, financing and selling.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of middlemen in the marketing of farm produce is that they
options: buy produce in bulk from farmers
may hoard produce and increase prices to consumers
questions.explanation: Middlemen perform useful services but may exploit farmers and consumers through hoarding and high margins.

questions.stem: Cooperative marketing helps farmers mainly by
options: increasing their bargaining power through collective selling
questions.explanation: Selling together lowers costs and gives better prices.

questions.stem: Agricultural insurance is a scheme that
options: lends money to farmers without interest
compensates farmers for losses due to insured risks such as fire, flood and disease
questions.explanation: Farmers pay premiums and receive compensation for losses covered by the policy.

questions.stem: The amount a farmer pays periodically to an insurance company to keep a policy in force is called the
questions.explanation: The premium is paid by the insured; the indemnity is the compensation paid after a loss.

questions.stem: Agricultural extension is mainly concerned with
options: educating farmers on improved farming practices and passing their problems to researchers
questions.explanation: Extension links research and farmers through education and feedback.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a group method of agricultural extension?
questions.explanation: Demonstrations, field days and meetings reach groups; radio and newspapers are mass methods, visits are individual methods.

questions.stem: The correct order of stages in the adoption of a new farm practice is
questions.explanation: Farmers first become aware, then interested, evaluate, try on a small scale and finally adopt.

questions.stem: When a moist soil sample is rubbed between the fingers, it feels smooth and sticky and can be rolled into a thin thread. The soil is
questions.explanation: Clay particles are fine and plastic when moist; sand feels gritty and cannot be rolled.

questions.stem: In a soil pit, the dark-coloured top layer rich in humus is the
questions.explanation: The A horizon contains most organic matter and is darkest.

questions.stem: A student added dilute hydrochloric acid to a rock specimen and observed effervescence. The rock is most likely
questions.explanation: Limestone (calcium carbonate) reacts with acid releasing carbon dioxide bubbles.

questions.topic: Practical: Laboratory work on physical properties of soil
questions.stem: Equal masses of sand, loam and clay were placed in funnels and equal volumes of water poured on them. The funnel that collected the LEAST water after 30 minutes contained
questions.explanation: Clay has the highest water-holding capacity, so least water drains through it.

questions.topic: Practical: Laboratory work on physical properties of soil
questions.stem: A dry soil sample of 50 g was heated strongly in a crucible until constant mass and weighed 46 g. The percentage of organic matter (loss on ignition) in the soil is
questions.explanation: Loss = 50 - 46 = 4 g; percentage = 4/50 x 100 = 8%.

questions.topic: Practical: Laboratory work on physical properties of soil
questions.stem: When a soil sample is shaken in a measuring cylinder of water and allowed to settle, the layer at the bottom consists of
questions.explanation: Heavier, larger particles settle first; clay settles last and humus floats.

questions.topic: Practical: Laboratory work on chemical properties of soil
questions.stem: The instrument used to measure soil pH directly is the
questions.explanation: A pH meter (or indicator papers/solutions) measures acidity or alkalinity.

questions.stem: Which of the following items is part of a sprinkler irrigation system?
options: Rotating nozzle, lateral pipe and pump
questions.explanation: Sprinkler systems use a pump, main and lateral pipes, risers and nozzles.

questions.stem: The farm tool that has a long handle and a flat, slightly curved blade, used for digging and loading soil, is the
questions.explanation: A shovel lifts and moves soil and other loose materials.

questions.topic: Practical: Tractor and animal drawn implements
questions.stem: Which of the following is an animal-drawn implement?
questions.explanation: Ox ploughs and ridgers are pulled by draught animals; the others are tractor-powered.

questions.topic: Practical: Harvesting, processing and storage equipment
questions.stem: A cassava grater is a processing equipment used in the production of
questions.explanation: Peeled cassava is grated, pressed, fermented and fried to make garri.

questions.topic: Practical: Harvesting, processing and storage equipment
questions.stem: A silo is a structure used for
options: storing grains in bulk or making silage
questions.explanation: Silos store grain or chopped green fodder (silage).

questions.stem: The part of a tractor that transfers power from the engine to drive implements such as rotavators is the
questions.explanation: The PTO shaft drives rotary implements; the drawbar only pulls trailed implements.

questions.topic: Practical: Uses and maintenance of horticultural tools and implements
questions.stem: Secateurs are used in horticulture for
options: pruning small branches and cutting flowers
questions.explanation: Secateurs (pruning shears) make clean cuts on stems up to finger thickness.

questions.stem: A burdizzo is used on the farm for
questions.explanation: The burdizzo crushes the spermatic cords without breaking the skin.

questions.stem: A drenching gun is used to
options: administer liquid medicine orally to livestock
questions.explanation: Drenching guns deliver measured doses of liquid dewormers into the mouth.

questions.stem: Ranging poles are used in farm surveying to
options: mark points and keep survey lines straight
questions.explanation: Red and white ranging poles are placed to mark stations and align straight lines.

questions.topic: Practical: Seeds, seedlings, fruits and storage organs of crops
questions.stem: Which of the following crops stores food in a corm?
questions.explanation: Cocoyam has a corm; cassava and sweet potato have root tubers and onion has a bulb.

questions.topic: Practical: Main pests and diseases of crops
questions.stem: A specimen of cocoa pod shows brown to black patches that spread over the pod surface with whitish fungal growth. The disease is
questions.explanation: Black pod is a fungal disease showing spreading dark lesions with white sporulation.

questions.topic: Practical: Planting dates, seed rates, plant population and seed quality tests
questions.stem: In a germination test, 100 cowpea seeds were planted and 85 germinated. The germination percentage is
questions.explanation: Germination % = (85/100) x 100 = 85%.

questions.topic: Practical: Planting dates, seed rates, plant population and seed quality tests
questions.stem: Maize was planted at 90 cm x 30 cm with two seeds per hole. The number of seeds required per hectare (assuming 100% germination) is

questions.topic: Practical: Seedbed preparation and crop husbandry operations
questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct sequence of operations in preparing a seedbed?
questions.explanation: Land is first cleared, then ploughed, harrowed to fine tilth and ridged.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-timber forest product?
questions.explanation: Honey, mushrooms, fruits, chewing sticks and bush meat are non-timber forest products.

questions.topic: Practical: Methods of propagation of horticultural plants
questions.stem: The plant part inserted onto a rootstock during grafting is the
questions.explanation: The scion is the upper part from the desired variety; the stock provides the root system.

questions.stem: Which of the following weeds is a sedge?
questions.explanation: Cyperus has triangular stems and tubers; Tridax and Euphorbia are broadleaves and Imperata is a grass.

questions.topic: Practical: Common breeds and types of animals
questions.stem: A breed of goat with a reddish-brown coat, common in northern Nigeria and valued for its skin, is the
questions.explanation: Red Sokoto goats produce high quality skins; Yankasa is a sheep breed.

questions.topic: Practical: Major internal organs of farm animals
questions.stem: The organ in a slaughtered fowl that has a thick muscular wall and a hard inner lining containing grit is the
questions.explanation: The gizzard grinds food with grit; the proventriculus is the glandular stomach.

questions.stem: Blood collected from abattoirs can be processed into
questions.explanation: Dried blood (blood meal) is a protein supplement for feeds and a fertiliser.

questions.topic: Practical: Animal feeds and feed stuffs
questions.stem: Bone meal is added to livestock rations mainly as a source of
questions.explanation: Bone meal supplies minerals for bone formation and eggshell.

questions.topic: Practical: Main pests and parasites of farm animals
questions.stem: Ticks are harmful to cattle mainly because they
options: eat the grass in the pasture
suck blood and transmit diseases such as babesiosis
questions.explanation: Ticks cause blood loss, damage hides and transmit diseases such as babesiosis (redwater) and heartwater.

questions.topic: Practical: Main pests and parasites of farm animals
questions.stem: The liver fluke of cattle and sheep completes its life cycle in an intermediate host which is a
questions.explanation: Fasciola larvae develop in Lymnaea snails before encysting on grass.

questions.stem: Foot-and-mouth disease in cattle is characterised by
options: blisters in the mouth and on the feet, with excessive salivation and lameness
questions.explanation: FMD is a viral disease with vesicles on mouth, feet and teats.

questions.topic: Practical: Routine management practices in farm animals
questions.stem: Debeaking in poultry is done mainly to
questions.explanation: Trimming the beak reduces pecking injuries and feed wastage.

questions.topic: Practical: Routine management practices in farm animals
questions.stem: The removal of horn buds in young calves to prevent horn growth is called
questions.explanation: Disbudding (dehorning at an early age) uses a hot iron or caustic paste.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods of fish preservation is most widely used by artisanal fishermen in West Africa?
questions.explanation: Smoking over wood fires in kilns is common and cheap; canning and freezing need more capital.

questions.stem: A gill net catches fish by
options: scooping them from the water surface
luring them with bait on a hook
entangling them by the gills as they try to swim through the mesh
questions.explanation: Fish pass their heads through the mesh and are caught behind the gill covers.

questions.topic: Problems of agricultural development and possible solutions
questions.stem:
(a) State five problems of agricultural development in Nigeria. [5 marks]
(b) Suggest one solution to each of the problems stated in (a). [5 marks]
(c) Explain four ways in which the government can assist farmers to increase food production. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Any five, 1 mark each: inadequate credit/capital; poor storage and processing facilities; land tenure problems; poor rural infrastructure (roads, electricity); pests and diseases; inadequate extension services; high cost of inputs; poor marketing/price fluctuations; insecurity on farms; rural-urban migration/ageing farm population; dependence on rainfall
5 marks: (b) Matching solution to each problem, 1 mark each, e.g. credit - agricultural loans at low interest; storage - silos/cold rooms/processing industries; land tenure - land reform; infrastructure - rural roads and electrification; pests - supply of agrochemicals/IPM; extension - recruit and train extension agents; inputs - subsidies; marketing - cooperatives/guaranteed minimum price; insecurity - farm security programmes
8 marks: (c) Any four, 2 marks each (point 1 + explanation 1): provision of credit/loans; subsidy on fertilisers, seeds and agrochemicals; funding research institutes to develop improved varieties; extension services to teach farmers; provision of rural infrastructure; price support/guaranteed minimum price; irrigation schemes and river basin development; establishing storage and processing facilities; agricultural insurance
questions.explanation: (a) Problems include lack of credit, poor storage, land tenure, poor rural infrastructure, pests and diseases, inadequate extension, high input costs and marketing problems. (b) Solutions: low-interest loans, silos and processing plants, land reform, rural roads, pest management, more extension agents, input subsidies and cooperative marketing. (c) Government can give credit and input subsidies, fund research for improved varieties, strengthen extension, build infrastructure and irrigation schemes, guarantee minimum prices and provide insurance.

questions.stem:
(a) Define weathering. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four factors of soil formation. [8 marks]
(c) Describe the features of the A, B and C horizons of a typical soil profile. [6 marks]
(d) State two importance of a deep soil profile to crop production. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The breakdown (disintegration and decomposition) of rocks into smaller particles by physical, chemical and biological agents
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: parent material - determines texture and mineral content; climate - rainfall and temperature control rate of weathering and leaching; living organisms - plants, animals and microorganisms add humus and break rocks; topography - affects drainage, erosion and depth of soil; time - age determines degree of development of horizons
2 marks: (c) A horizon (topsoil): dark due to humus, loose, most biological activity and roots, zone of eluviation (leaching)
2 marks: (c) B horizon (subsoil): lighter colour, more compact, accumulation of clay, iron and aluminium oxides (illuviation), few roots
2 marks: (c) C horizon: weathered parent material, little or no organic matter, lies on bedrock
2 marks: (d) Any two, 1 mark each: allows deep root penetration and good anchorage; stores more water and nutrients; better drainage; supports tree crops
questions.explanation: (a) Weathering is the breakdown of rocks into smaller particles by physical, chemical and biological processes. (b) Parent material determines texture and minerals; climate controls weathering and leaching; organisms add humus and break rocks; topography affects drainage and erosion; time allows horizons to develop. (c) The A horizon is dark, rich in humus and roots; the B horizon is compact and receives leached clay and oxides; the C horizon is partly weathered parent material. (d) A deep profile allows deep rooting and holds more water and nutrients.

questions.stem:
(a) State the functions of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in crops, and one deficiency symptom of each. [9 marks]
(b) A farmer wants to supply 90 kg of nitrogen to one hectare of maize using urea (46% N). Calculate, to the nearest kilogram, the quantity of urea required. [3 marks]
(c) State three ways by which soil fertility can be maintained other than by using inorganic fertilisers. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Nitrogen: promotes vegetative growth / formation of proteins and chlorophyll
1 mark: (a) N deficiency: yellowing (chlorosis) of older leaves / stunted growth
2 marks: (a) Phosphorus: root development / flowering, fruiting and seed formation / early maturity / energy transfer (ATP)
1 mark: (a) P deficiency: purplish colour of leaves / poor root growth / delayed maturity
2 marks: (a) Potassium: disease resistance / strong stems / carbohydrate formation and translocation / fruit quality
1 mark: (a) K deficiency: scorching or browning of leaf margins / weak stems and lodging
1 mark: (b) Quantity of urea = 90 / 0.46 (or 90 x 100/46)
2 marks: (b) = 195.65, approximately 196 kg of urea
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: crop rotation including legumes; application of farmyard manure/compost; green manuring; mulching; cover cropping; bush fallowing; liming of acid soils; controlling erosion; avoiding bush burning
questions.explanation: (a) Nitrogen promotes leafy growth and protein formation (deficiency: yellowing of older leaves); phosphorus promotes roots, flowering and maturity (deficiency: purpling and poor roots); potassium aids disease resistance, strong stems and starch movement (deficiency: scorched leaf margins). (b) Urea = 90 / 0.46 = 195.65, about 196 kg. (c) Fertility can be maintained by crop rotation with legumes, manuring and composting, green manuring, mulching, cover cropping, fallowing and liming.

questions.stem:
(a) Define irrigation and drainage. [4 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of irrigation and state one advantage of each. [9 marks]
(c) State five reasons for draining agricultural land. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Irrigation: artificial application of water to the soil to supplement rainfall for crop growth
2 marks: (a) Drainage: removal of excess water from the soil surface or the root zone
9 marks: (b) Any three methods, 3 marks each (2 description + 1 advantage): surface/furrow - water flows by gravity along furrows between ridges, cheap; basin/flood - field divided into level basins flooded with water, suitable for rice; sprinkler - water under pressure sprayed through nozzles like rain, useful on uneven land/light soils; drip/trickle - water delivered slowly to root zone through pipes and emitters, saves water and reduces weeds; sub-surface - water supplied through underground pipes, little evaporation
5 marks: (c) Any five, 1 mark each: improves soil aeration; prevents waterlogging and root rot; warms the soil faster; encourages deep root growth; improves activity of soil microorganisms; makes tillage and machinery use easier; removes excess salts; increases range of crops; reclaims swamps
questions.explanation: (a) Irrigation is the artificial supply of water to crops; drainage is removal of excess water. (b) Furrow irrigation lets water flow by gravity between ridges and is cheap; basin irrigation floods level basins and suits rice; sprinkler irrigation sprays water under pressure, suiting uneven land; drip irrigation applies water drop by drop at roots, saving water. (c) Drainage improves aeration, prevents waterlogging and root rot, warms soil, allows deeper rooting, encourages microorganisms and eases machinery use.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four tractor-drawn implements and state one use of each. [8 marks]
(b) State five routine maintenance practices for a farm tractor. [5 marks]
(c) State five safety precautions to be observed when operating farm machinery. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each (1 name + 1 use): disc plough - primary tillage/turning soil; harrow - breaking clods and levelling; ridger - making ridges; planter - planting seeds; boom sprayer - spraying chemicals; cultivator - weeding/loosening soil; trailer - transporting materials; mower - cutting grass; fertiliser distributor - applying fertiliser
5 marks: (b) Any five, 1 mark each: check engine oil level daily; check radiator water/coolant; check tyre pressure; grease moving parts; clean or replace air filter; check battery water and terminals; change oil and filters at recommended hours; tighten loose nuts and bolts; check fuel level and fuel filter; wash after use
5 marks: (c) Any five, 1 mark each: operator should be trained; read manufacturer's manual; do not carry passengers; avoid loose clothing; stop engine before repairs/adjustment; never refuel with engine running or near fire; avoid steep slopes and sharp turns at speed; keep guards on PTO shafts; use protective equipment; keep children away
questions.explanation: (a) Disc plough turns the soil; harrow breaks clods; ridger forms ridges; planter sows seeds; boom sprayer applies chemicals. (b) Daily checks of oil, coolant, tyres, battery and fuel, greasing moving parts, cleaning the air filter, changing oil at intervals and tightening bolts. (c) Trained operators only, no passengers, no loose clothing, stop the engine before adjustments, no refuelling with engine running, care on slopes and guards on PTO shafts.

questions.stem: Using maize as an example, describe its cultivation under the following headings: (a) botanical name and ecological requirements; (b) land preparation; (c) planting (method, spacing, seed rate); (d) fertiliser application; (e) two pests and two diseases and their control; (f) harvesting and storage. [18 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Zea mays; requires well-drained fertile loamy soil, rainfall of about 600-1200 mm well distributed, warm temperatures, full sunlight
2 marks: (b) Clear the land, plough and harrow to fine tilth; ridge or plant on the flat
3 marks: (c) Plant 2-3 seeds per hole at 3-5 cm depth and thin to 1-2 plants; spacing e.g. 75 cm x 25 cm (one plant) or 90 cm x 30-45 cm (two plants); seed rate about 20-25 kg/ha
2 marks: (d) Apply NPK (e.g. 15:15:15) at planting or 2 weeks after planting and top-dress with urea/sulphate of ammonia at 4-6 weeks; ring or band placement
2 marks: (e) Pests: stem borer; armyworm (including fall armyworm); grasshoppers; weevils in storage (any two)
2 marks: (e) Control of pests: insecticides; early planting; crop rotation; destroying stubble; resistant varieties
2 marks: (e) Diseases: maize streak virus; leaf blight; rust; smut; downy mildew (any two), controlled by resistant varieties, fungicides, crop rotation, removing infected plants
3 marks: (f) Green maize harvested about 10-12 weeks; dry grain at 16-20 weeks when husks dry and kernels hard; dry cobs, shell and store in clean, dry, ventilated cribs/silos/bags with storage chemicals
questions.explanation: (a) Maize (Zea mays) needs fertile, well-drained loamy soil, warm temperatures, full sun and moderate, well-distributed rainfall. (b) The land is cleared, ploughed and harrowed, then ridged or left flat. (c) 2-3 seeds per hole at 3-5 cm depth, spaced e.g. 75 cm x 25 cm, thinned later; seed rate about 20-25 kg/ha. (d) NPK at or soon after planting with urea top-dressing at 4-6 weeks. (e) Pests such as stem borers and armyworms are controlled with insecticides, early planting and rotation; diseases such as maize streak and leaf blight with resistant varieties and sanitation. (f) Harvest green maize at about 3 months and dry grain at 4-5 months; dry, shell and store in clean, ventilated cribs or silos.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a pest and a disease of crops. [2 marks]
(b) Describe the damage caused by each of the following pests and state one method of control for each: (i) variegated grasshopper; (ii) cowpea bruchid; (iii) rodents in storage. [9 marks]
(c) Explain the meaning of integrated pest management (IPM) and state three of its advantages. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A pest is an organism (insect, rodent, bird, nematode) that damages crops directly by feeding; a disease is an abnormal condition of the plant caused by a pathogen (fungus, bacterium, virus) or deficiency that impairs its normal functioning
3 marks: (b)(i) Variegated grasshopper (Zonocerus) - defoliates leaves of cassava and other crops and bark of stems, reducing photosynthesis; control by insecticide spraying, hand picking/destroying egg pods, clean weeding
3 marks: (b)(ii) Bruchid - larvae bore into and feed inside stored cowpea seeds, leaving holes, reducing weight, quality and viability; control by drying properly, hermetic (airtight) storage, approved storage insecticides
3 marks: (b)(iii) Rodents - eat and contaminate stored produce with droppings and urine, damage bags; control by rat-proof stores, baits/traps, cleanliness
4 marks: (c) IPM is the combined use of several compatible methods (cultural, biological, resistant varieties, physical and minimal chemical) to keep pests below economic injury level with least harm to the environment
3 marks: (c) Any three advantages, 1 mark each: reduces pesticide use and cost; reduces pollution and residues in food; conserves natural enemies; delays pest resistance; sustainable
questions.explanation: (a) Pests feed on and damage crops; diseases are disorders caused by pathogens. (b) Grasshoppers defoliate crops, controlled by insecticides and destruction of egg pods; bruchids bore into stored cowpea, controlled by drying and airtight storage; rodents eat and foul stored produce, controlled by rat-proof stores and traps. (c) IPM combines cultural, biological, resistant-variety and limited chemical control to keep pests below damaging levels; it reduces cost and pollution, conserves natural enemies and slows resistance.

questions.stem:
(a) State four harmful effects and two beneficial effects of weeds. [6 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of weed control, stating one advantage of each. [9 marks]
(c) Give the botanical names of three common weeds of farmland in West Africa. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Harmful, any four, 1 mark each: compete with crops for nutrients, water, light and space; harbour pests and diseases; reduce yield and quality; increase cost of production; some are parasitic (Striga); some poisonous to livestock; block irrigation channels
2 marks: (a) Beneficial, any two, 1 mark each: control erosion as cover; add organic matter; some are used as livestock feed or medicinal herbs; indicate soil fertility
9 marks: (b) Any three methods, 3 marks each (2 description + 1 advantage): manual - hand pulling, hoeing, slashing, cheap and selective; mechanical - tractor-drawn cultivators/rotary weeders, fast on large farms; chemical - herbicides (pre- or post-emergence), saves labour and time; cultural - crop rotation, cover crops, mulching, proper spacing, no chemical pollution; biological - using organisms such as insects to suppress weeds, cheap and long-lasting
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: Imperata cylindrica; Cyperus rotundus; Tridax procumbens; Chromolaena odorata; Euphorbia heterophylla; Striga hermonthica; Talinum triangulare; Panicum maximum; Sida acuta
questions.explanation: (a) Weeds compete with crops, harbour pests, lower yield and raise costs, while they can also protect soil, add organic matter and serve as feed or medicine. (b) Manual weeding is cheap and selective; mechanical weeding is fast; herbicides save labour; cultural methods such as mulching and cover crops avoid pollution. (c) Imperata cylindrica, Cyperus rotundus and Chromolaena odorata.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the procedure for propagating a plant by marcotting (air layering). [8 marks]
(b) State four advantages of vegetative propagation. [4 marks]
(c) Name three ornamental plants used for hedges and three used as lawn grasses. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Select a healthy, semi-hardwood branch of pencil thickness on the parent plant
2 marks: (a) Remove a ring of bark about 2-3 cm wide around the branch, scraping off the cambium
2 marks: (a) Cover the ringed portion with moist rooting medium (soil/sawdust/coir), possibly with rooting hormone, wrap in polythene and tie both ends
2 marks: (a) Keep moist; after roots appear (4-8 weeks) cut the branch below the roots and plant in a pot or nursery
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: offspring identical to parent (true to type); earlier flowering/fruiting; plants that produce no viable seeds can be propagated; combines good qualities of stock and scion (grafting); faster establishment
3 marks: (c) Hedges, any three: Ixora; Duranta; Hibiscus; Bougainvillea; Acalypha; Croton; Thuja
3 marks: (c) Lawn grasses, any three: carpet grass (Axonopus compressus); Bahama/Bermuda grass (Cynodon dactylon); Paspalum; Zoysia; St Augustine grass
questions.explanation: (a) A ring of bark is removed from a healthy branch, the wound is covered with moist rooting medium and wrapped in polythene; after roots form, the branch is cut and potted. (b) Vegetative propagation gives true-to-type plants, earlier fruiting and allows propagation of seedless plants. (c) Hedges: Ixora, Duranta, Hibiscus. Lawns: carpet grass, Bahama grass and Paspalum.

questions.stem:
(a) What is agro-forestry? [2 marks]
(b) Describe the taungya system and alley cropping. [8 marks]
(c) State four advantages of agro-forestry to the farmer and the environment. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) A land-use system in which trees or shrubs are deliberately grown together with crops and/or animals on the same land
4 marks: (b) Taungya: farmers are allowed to grow food crops between rows of young forest tree seedlings in a forest plantation; they tend the trees until the canopy closes, after which they move to a new site
4 marks: (b) Alley cropping: food crops are grown in alleys between hedgerows of fast-growing leguminous trees/shrubs (e.g. Leucaena, Gliricidia); hedgerows are pruned regularly and prunings used as mulch/green manure
8 marks: (c) Any four, 2 marks each: improves soil fertility (nitrogen fixation, litter); controls erosion; provides fuelwood, timber, fodder and fruits; diversifies income; reduces cost of plantation establishment; conserves biodiversity; acts as windbreak; reduces pressure on natural forests
questions.explanation: (a) Agro-forestry combines trees with crops and/or livestock on the same land. (b) In taungya, farmers crop between young plantation trees and tend them until the canopy closes. In alley cropping, crops grow between hedgerows of legumes such as Leucaena whose prunings serve as mulch and green manure. (c) Agro-forestry improves soil fertility, controls erosion, provides wood, fodder and fruit, diversifies income and reduces pressure on forests.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following terms: (i) oestrous cycle; (ii) gestation period; (iii) parturition. [6 marks]
(b) State the gestation period of the cow, sow, ewe and doe (rabbit). [4 marks]
(c) State four signs of heat in farm animals. [4 marks]
(d) State four ways of caring for a pregnant sow. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Oestrous cycle: the period from one heat (oestrus) to the next in a non-pregnant female, e.g. about 21 days in cows and sows
2 marks: (a)(ii) Gestation: the period from fertilisation/conception to birth
2 marks: (a)(iii) Parturition: the act or process of giving birth
1 mark: (b) Cow: about 283 days (approximately 9 months)
1 mark: (b) Sow: about 114 days (3 months, 3 weeks, 3 days)
1 mark: (b) Ewe: about 147-150 days (about 5 months)
1 mark: (b) Doe (rabbit): about 30-32 days
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: restlessness; mounting others and standing to be mounted; swollen, reddened vulva; mucus discharge; frequent urination; loss of appetite; bellowing/grunting; drop in milk yield
4 marks: (d) Any four, 1 mark each: feed a balanced ration with adequate protein, minerals and vitamins; provide clean water; deworm and treat against parasites; separate from other pigs late in pregnancy; provide a clean disinfected farrowing pen with farrowing crate/guard rails and bedding; regular exercise; avoid rough handling
questions.explanation: (a) The oestrous cycle is the interval between successive heats; gestation is the time from conception to birth; parturition is giving birth. (b) Cow about 283 days, sow 114 days, ewe about 150 days, rabbit about 31 days. (c) Restlessness, mounting, swollen red vulva, mucus discharge, frequent urination and reduced appetite. (d) A pregnant sow needs a balanced ration, clean water, deworming, separation and a clean farrowing pen with guard rails and bedding.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the deep litter system of keeping poultry. [6 marks]
(b) State three advantages and three disadvantages of the battery cage system. [6 marks]
(c) Outline the management of day-old broiler chicks during the brooding period. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Birds are kept in a house with a solid floor covered with litter material such as wood shavings, rice husks or sawdust, 5-15 cm deep
2 marks: (a) Birds move freely within the house; feeders, drinkers and laying nests are provided
2 marks: (a) Litter is turned regularly and kept dry; the house is well ventilated with wire-mesh sides and a roof that keeps out rain
3 marks: (b) Advantages, any three, 1 mark each: high stocking density/uses less space; clean eggs; easy record keeping and culling; reduced cannibalism and diseases spread through droppings; less feed wastage; easy collection of eggs
3 marks: (b) Disadvantages, any three: high capital cost; cage layer fatigue/leg problems; birds cannot exercise; welfare concerns; fly and odour problems if droppings not removed; needs constant supply of feed and water
6 marks: (c) Any six, 1 mark each: clean and disinfect brooder house before arrival; provide heat (brooder/lamp/charcoal pot) at about 32-35 degrees C in the first week, reducing weekly; provide litter and chick guard; give clean water with glucose/vitamins on arrival; feed broiler starter mash; adequate ventilation and light; vaccinate (e.g. Newcastle, Gumboro) as scheduled; observe chicks' behaviour to adjust heat; footbath at entrance
questions.explanation: (a) In the deep litter system birds are housed on a floor covered with dry litter, move freely, and are given feeders, drinkers and nests in a well-ventilated house. (b) Battery cages save space, give clean eggs, ease records and reduce disease spread, but are costly, restrict movement and cause welfare and leg problems. (c) Brooding involves a disinfected house, a heat source at about 32-35 degrees C reduced weekly, chick guards, clean water with glucose, starter mash, ventilation and a vaccination programme.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a roughage and a concentrate, giving two examples of each. [6 marks]
(b) A farmer wishes to prepare 100 kg of a ration containing 16% crude protein from maize (8% CP) and groundnut cake (40% CP). Using the Pearson square method, calculate the quantity of each ingredient required. [8 marks]
(c) State four functions of water in the body of farm animals. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Roughage: bulky, high fibre (above about 18%), low digestible nutrients
1 mark: (a) Examples: hay, silage, straw, fresh grass (any two)
2 marks: (a) Concentrate: low fibre, high in energy or protein, highly digestible
1 mark: (a) Examples: maize, groundnut cake, soybean meal, fish meal (any two)
2 marks: (b) Draw square: 16 in the centre; maize 8 and groundnut cake 40 at the left corners
2 marks: (b) Parts of maize = 40 - 16 = 24; parts of groundnut cake = 16 - 8 = 8; total = 32 parts
2 marks: (b) Maize = 24/32 x 100 = 75 kg
2 marks: (b) Groundnut cake = 8/32 x 100 = 25 kg
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: medium for chemical reactions; transport of nutrients and wastes; regulation of body temperature; lubrication of joints; component of body fluids, milk and eggs; aids digestion and excretion
questions.explanation: (a) Roughages such as hay and silage are bulky and fibrous; concentrates such as maize and groundnut cake are low in fibre and rich in energy or protein. (b) Pearson square: maize parts = 40 - 16 = 24; groundnut cake parts = 16 - 8 = 8; total 32. Maize = 24/32 x 100 = 75 kg; groundnut cake = 25 kg. Check: 0.75 x 8 + 0.25 x 40 = 6 + 10 = 16% CP. (c) Water is a medium for reactions, transports substances, regulates temperature and lubricates joints.

questions.stem:
(a) For each of the following diseases, state the causal organism (type), two symptoms and one control measure: (i) Newcastle disease of poultry; (ii) trypanosomiasis of cattle; (iii) coccidiosis of poultry. [12 marks]
(b) State six general preventive measures against diseases on a livestock farm. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a)(i) Newcastle disease - virus (paramyxovirus)
2 marks: (a)(i) Symptoms: gasping/respiratory distress, greenish diarrhoea, twisting of neck, paralysis, sudden deaths, drop in egg production (any two)
1 mark: (a)(i) Control: vaccination; isolation/destruction of sick birds; farm hygiene
1 mark: (a)(ii) Trypanosomiasis - protozoan (Trypanosoma), transmitted by tsetse fly
2 marks: (a)(ii) Symptoms: intermittent fever, anaemia, progressive weight loss/emaciation, swollen lymph nodes, abortion, lacrimation (any two)
1 mark: (a)(ii) Control: trypanocidal drugs; tsetse control (clearing bushes, traps, insecticides); trypanotolerant breeds
1 mark: (a)(iii) Coccidiosis - protozoan (Eimeria species)
2 marks: (a)(iii) Symptoms: bloody/watery diarrhoea, ruffled feathers, droopiness, loss of appetite, death in young birds (any two)
1 mark: (a)(iii) Control: coccidiostats in feed or water; keeping litter dry; avoiding overcrowding
6 marks: (b) Any six, 1 mark each: vaccination; quarantine of new animals; isolation of sick animals; good sanitation and disinfection; footbaths; balanced feeding; clean water; avoid overcrowding; good ventilation; routine deworming and dipping; proper disposal of carcasses; buying stock from disease-free sources; regular veterinary inspection
questions.explanation: (a) Newcastle disease is viral, causing gasping, greenish diarrhoea and twisted necks; it is prevented by vaccination. Trypanosomiasis is caused by Trypanosoma spread by tsetse flies, causing fever, anaemia and wasting; it is controlled with trypanocides, tsetse control and trypanotolerant breeds. Coccidiosis is caused by Eimeria, giving bloody droppings and droopiness; coccidiostats and dry litter control it. (b) Vaccination, quarantine, isolation, sanitation, footbaths, good feeding, avoiding overcrowding, deworming, dipping and proper carcass disposal.

questions.stem:
(a) State four factors to be considered in selecting a site for a fish pond. [4 marks]
(b) Describe four management practices in a fish pond after stocking. [8 marks]
(c) Describe two methods of preserving fish. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
